attacks.claim: Vector Store holds all derived customer data (chunks, embeddings, per-tenant collections) and is provisioned only in us-east-2, with no EU region available. The plan re-embeds ~41M chunks into it in week 2 and dual-writes new documents, so customer-derived data would leave the EU during the build, before any residency check. This breaks the agreed DPA constraint, and the copy cannot be cleanly undone.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview and currently provisioned in us-east-2, with EU regions on Nimbus's GA roadmap." / "Week 2: re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store; dual-write new documents."

attacks.claim: The 4,100-case regression suite, which the constraints name as the release gate for any model change, is deferred to week 6+, after the week-4 cutover. Every tenant would move to a new model and prompt set without passing the gate.
attacks.evidence: "so the full regression suite run moves to post-migration hardening (week 6+) rather than blocking cutover."

attacks.claim: Weeks 3 and 5 destroy the rollback path before cutover is validated. Week 3 releases the A100 reservation and deletes fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters, both before the week-4 cutover and the week-6+ regression run. Week 5 removes pgvector, vLLM manifests and the GPU node pool, so the only copy of the per-tenant retrieval data becomes the Nimbus collection, and restoring it would require re-embedding ~41M chunks.
attacks.evidence: "Week 3: release the A100 reservation ... and delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage" / "Week 5: remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool from Terraform."

attacks.claim: Quality parity is claimed from a 25-question blind comparison by two staff lawyers. That sample is too small and unrepresentative to support a parity conclusion for a model change, especially across practice areas, and it does not replace the 4,100-case gate.
attacks.evidence: "ran 25 representative questions from the support inbox through both stacks ... Atlas-L was preferred in 19 of 25 and tied in 3. This confirms quality parity or better"

attacks.claim: Practice-area behaviour previously carried by LoRA adapters is assumed to transfer to system prompts, but the prompts are only drafted in week 1 and no evaluation of them is described. Behaviour equivalence is unverified.
attacks.evidence: "practice-area behaviour that lived in LoRA adapters moves into per-practice system prompts (drafted in week 1 by the applied team)."

attacks.claim: Embeddings are generated by embed-3 with no stated region. Only generation is pinned to eu-west-1, so the processing location of customer-derived chunks is unconfirmed.
attacks.evidence: "Embeddings: Nimbus embed-3 (1,536 dims), called from the ingest workers." (no region stated)

attacks.claim: Inference, embeddings, retrieval and prompt behaviour all depend on one vendor with no fallback or abstraction. The old stack is decommissioned before any fallback is proven. There is also no export path for vectors or model artifacts, so exit would require re-embedding and re-training.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any multi-provider path, export requirement or documented exit procedure. "Week 5: remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool from Terraform."

attacks.claim: Cutover moves all tenants at once, with no canary or staged rollout and no per-tenant rollback trigger. Dual-write in week 2 has no stated source-of-truth or reconciliation rule. A partial or failed cutover could not be reverted safely.
attacks.evidence: "Week 4: cut all tenants over to Nimbus (generation + retrieval)." / "dual-write new documents" (no reconciliation rule)

attacks.claim: No deletion or erasure procedure is specified for tenant documents, chunks and embeddings in Nimbus Vector Store. Offboarding or DPA-driven erasure is therefore unsupported, and the week-5 removal of pgvector eliminates the existing deletion mechanism.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: tenant deletion/erasure procedure for Vector Store collections. "Week 5: remove pgvector ..."

attacks.claim: Retention terms for embed-3 calls and Vector Store collections are not stated. The ZDR addendum is cited only in the generation bullet, so derived-data retention by the vendor is not shown to be covered.
attacks.evidence: "Zero data retention is enabled on our org account (signed addendum, ref NMB-ZDR-2291)." / ABSENT: retention terms for embed-3 and Vector Store

attacks.claim: Tenant isolation in the shared Nimbus org relies on a tenant-scoped API key in a preview product. No isolation testing or documentation is cited, so equivalence with per-tenant pgvector schemas is unverified.
attacks.evidence: "Tenant isolation in Vector Store uses one collection per tenant with a tenant-scoped API key, mirroring today's per-tenant pgvector schemas."

attacks.claim: Retrieval is built on a public-preview managed store, and there is no throughput, scale or reliability evidence for re-embedding ~41M chunks or for serving production retrieval on it. Retrieval quality is also not measured separately from generation, so retrieval regressions could be hidden.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus Vector Store (managed) ... is in public preview" / "re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store"

attacks.claim: The cost after-state rests on a generation estimate with no stated basis (token volume, unit price or request mix). The $7,900 figure and the $9,550 total cannot be checked, and the savings case depends on them.
The 200k-context rationale is not measured. Latency evidence is time-to-first-token only, on an unspecified workload, with no end-to-end time or long-context answer quality.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus Atlas-L supports 200k context natively" / "Atlas-L p95 time-to-first-token measured at 640 ms"

attacks.claim: Rate-limit headroom compares average-based peak load with the contracted ceiling. It does not show the 120 req/s tier is in force, that bursts and retries fit, or that re-embedding load alongside production traffic fits.
attacks.evidence: "our peak is ~40 req/s; our contracted tier allows 120 req/s."

attacks.claim: Week 3 deletes fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters without confirming whether they were trained on customer data and whether DPA deletion or retention terms apply to them.
attacks.evidence: "delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage"

attacks.claim: The plan removes the only self-hostable inference path. A future on-prem or sovereign deployment requirement would need a rebuild. This should be recorded as a known constraint.
attacks.evidence: "Move generation + retrieval to Nimbus AI"; ABSENT: any retained self-hosted fallback.
